findings: operating_context_acceptance.py does not check q.claim(report['id']) for None before using review_claim['attempt_id']; hosted_cycle.run raises an explicit REVIEW_CLAIM_UNAVAILABLE for the same case. A None claim here surfaces as a TypeError — still fail-closed, but with an unclear reconciliation signal.

operating_context_acceptance.py has no BaseException handler around the model calls: on mid-cycle failure it writes no blocked.json and a claimed review stays in REVIEWING in the report queue (hosted_cycle.run marks it unavailable). The durable folder claim still forces manual reconciliation with no automatic retry, so this is an evidence/audit-clarity gap, not a safety hole.

operating_context_acceptance.py hardcodes day '2026-09-06' in the finalize() call; acceptable for a dated one-shot acceptance script bound to READINESS_HOSTED_ACCEPTANCE_20260906.json, but a later rerun would mislabel the report date.

hosted_cycle.run does not assert that the operator-supplied --root equals the running repository that model_call uses for canonical context (the acceptance route does assert this). Both are independently pinned to clean verified commits and both commits are recorded in the binding and operating context, so any divergence is auditable, but the packet's 'implementation' content could come from a different checkout than the canonical direction documents.

The acceptance route's orientation call reuses stage name 'continuation', so its artifacts are persisted as continuation.* despite being the orientation step; cosmetic, but slightly weakens artifact self-description for auditors.

envelope()'s task-packet checks (is_symlink, st_size) precede the read non-atomically, a minor TOCTOU window; low risk given the root-only supervised local execution context and immutable 0o600 packet files.

findings: SUGGESTION (verified, source-only) — orchestrator/hosted_context.py envelope(): verified_source defaults to None, so a hosted invocation can bind verified_source_commit: null with nothing distinguishing 'verification skipped' from 'verified absent'; build() also scans operating-context.json before the field is added, so scanned bytes differ from the bytes sent. Consequence: weakened source-identity binding on hosted turns. Affected task: hosted invocation assembly. Smallest correction: require an explicit commit or an explicit UNVERIFIED sentinel and set it before the scan.

SUGGESTION (verified, source-only) — orchestrator/hosted_context.py envelope(): the caller-supplied prompt is concatenated into the outbound body without a scan() pass; task_state is covered by build()'s packet scan but the prompt is not, making it the one unscanned path to the hosted model. Affected task: hosted invocation assembly. Smallest correction: scan the final composed body before returning.

SUGGESTION (verified, source-only) — orchestrator/reviewer_evidence.py collect() hosted branch: subprocess.TimeoutExpired or a missing systemctl binary propagates uncaught, aborting the entire collection and discarding already-collected historical records. Fail-closed (no false success) but not durable. Affected task: reviewer evidence collection. Smallest correction: catch per unit and append a COLLECTION_FAILED observation with execution_proven false.

SUGGESTION (verified, source-only) — orchestrator/reviewer_evidence.py validate(): request_id is derived from sort_keys=True serialization but scan() receives insertion-order bytes, so equivalent requests deduplicate to one id while producing different scanned artifacts. Affected task: evidence request identity/dedup. Smallest correction: scan the same canonical sorted serialization used for the hash.

SUGGESTION (verified, source-only) — orchestrator/hosted_context.py build(): the permitted_findings scope 'isles24-prediction' and the P001 proposal path are hard-coded; acceptable while ISLES is the only active campaign, but a second campaign's hosted turn would silently receive ISLES findings. Smallest correction: derive both from the bound task state before a second campaign activates.

VERIFIED fail-closed boundaries (source-only): build() raises FileNotFoundError on any missing canonical document; envelope() rejects absent, empty, symlinked, or oversized task packets (CURRENT_TASK_CONTEXT_REQUIRED / TASK_CONTEXT_PATH) before composing a hosted body; missing evidence sources record UNAVAILABLE rather than success; current_observations stays empty for non-hosted calls and non-runtime kinds; non-FileNotFoundError integrity failures propagate rather than degrade.

VERIFIED privacy filtering (source-only): hosted collection runs only fixed 'systemctl show' commands against fixed UNITS, retains only the ten allowlisted PROPERTIES (no Environment, no ExecStart, no stderr), always sets execution_proven false with status CURRENT_CONFIGURATION_ONLY, and every persistent record (request, per-source content, properties, response, operating context) passes through scan(); historical receipts are labeled HISTORICAL_DOCUMENT_NOT_CURRENT_EXECUTION_PROOF.

VERIFIED authority and approval preservation (source-only): the evidence request schema is closed (exact key set, enumerated kinds matching the directive's ten, bounded 500-char text, no request-selected paths or commands); frozen scientific artifacts carry non-authority dispositions (FROZEN_SPECIFICATION_NOT_LAUNCH_AUTHORITY, TASK_RECORD_NOT_AUTHORITY, DECISION_DEPENDENCIES_NOT_GRANTS, EVIDENCE_NOT_AUTHORITY); the precedence statement plus directive text keep patient launch, charter ratification, 047 landing/cleanup, reserved data, main merges, protected writer/reset, limiter activation, credentials and spending behind their named gates; recovery turns rebind the current canonical direction (fresh sha256, same document set and dispositions) while preserving the original prompt as non-overriding historical evidence, matching the operating direction's recovery semantics.

NOTE: no tests were executed; all findings come from reading the supplied source at the pinned commit. As written, the tests cover the closed request schema and dedup, UNAVAILABLE-not-success, stderr/property filtering, fixed-command enforcement, canonical rebinding on recovery, and empty-packet rejection.

findings: BLOCKER | orchestrator/hosted_context.py envelope() | verified from supplied source | Task-state binding lacks provenance and silently falls back to the parent directory: the candidate search (folder/post-execution-packet.json, folder/packet.json, then the parent's equivalents) means a recovery folder missing its own packet inherits the parent's stale pre-execution state, and the emitted envelope records neither the selected packet's path nor its sha256 (canonical documents are hashed; the bound task state is not). Consequence: a recovery invocation can act on superseded decision_inbox/executed_selection while appearing correctly bound, violating the approved direction's 'fresh invocation uses its explicitly bound current approved context'. Affected task: hosted driver/reviewer recovery. Smallest fix: record the resolved packet path and sha256 in the operating-context packet and require an explicit opt-in for parent-directory fallback.

BLOCKER | orchestrator/hosted_context.py envelope() | verified from supplied source | Source identity fails open: verified_source defaults to None and becomes the string 'UNVERIFIED', yet a full envelope is still built, scanned and returned for 'every real hosted model invocation'; both hosted-context tests exercise only this default path. Consequence: callers that omit the argument dispatch hosted turns with no source identity binding, only a passive label. Affected task: all hosted invocations. Smallest fix: make verified_source required, or raise unless an explicit allow_unverified flag is passed.

SUGGESTION | orchestrator/reviewer_evidence.py collect() | verified from supplied source | Only subprocess.TimeoutExpired and FileNotFoundError are caught around subprocess.run; a PermissionError or other OSError from systemctl aborts the entire collection and discards the already-assembled historical records instead of degrading that unit to COLLECTION_FAILED (tests cover only FileNotFoundError). Affected task: reviewer evidence collection. Smallest fix: broaden the except clause to OSError.

SUGGESTION | orchestrator/reviewer_evidence.py collect() | verified from supplied source | Evidence responses record request_id, timestamps and per-document sha256s but not the collector's own installed-source/directive version, so a reviewer receiving reviewer_evidence in a later immutable task packet cannot bind the response to the collector version that produced it, despite the directive's requirement to record supplied-evidence versions. Affected task: nightly review evidence chain. Smallest fix: include the collector's source commit/version in the result envelope.

SUGGESTION | orchestrator/hosted_context.py build() | inferred/untested | The frozen P001 specification is read via research_context.checked() and shipped with disposition FROZEN_SPECIFICATION_NOT_LAUNCH_AUTHORITY, hashing whatever bytes are currently on disk; the frozen-identity guarantee rests entirely on checked(), which is outside the supplied source. If checked() does not pin the recorded frozen hash, tampered spec content would be presented as frozen. Affected task: hosted context integrity for P001. Smallest fix: confirm checked() enforces the frozen binding, or compare the computed sha256 against the recorded frozen identity and fail closed on mismatch.

SUGGESTION (minor) | orchestrator/reviewer_evidence.py main()/collect() | verified from supplied source | The request-file is_symlink/size checks precede read_text (TOCTOU race, acceptable given trusted-operator-only execution), and hosted observations with nonzero systemctl returncode are still labeled CURRENT_CONFIGURATION_ONLY with possibly empty properties; the returncode is recorded so this is informational. Affected task: reviewer evidence collection. Smallest fix: re-stat after open or read via a file descriptor, and mark nonzero-returncode observations as degraded.
